memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he goes out to the river. Confront him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake." - Exodus 7:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God sends Moses to meet Pharaoh at the Nile in the early morning. This is deliberate. Pharaoh very likely came to the river for religious ritual — the Nile was worshipped as a god and was the source of Egypt's entire life and economy.

So God confronts him precisely there, at the place of his false worship, at the moment of his devotion.

God often confronts us at the point of our misplaced trust. Not to embarrass us, but because that is where the real battle is. The idol has to be named where it lives.

For one person that is money. For another it is career, reputation, a relationship, a substance, the approval of a parent. Anything we look to for life instead of God will eventually be met by God.

Notice Moses is told to carry the same staff. The evidence of God's power goes with him. He does not confront an idol empty-handed, and neither do we — we go in the authority of Christ, who has already disarmed every rival power (Col 2:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I looking to for life that only God can give?
2. Where has God been confronting me lately, and have I been avoiding it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, expose the things I trust in place of You. Meet me at my river and set me free. Amen.
